newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Petronas says Yankee bond launch around end-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Petronas says Yankee bond launch around end-Sept.

text.p: Malaysia state oil company Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) said on Thursday it planned to launch its planned Yankee bond issue in the last week of September or the first week of October.
But it said the amount and tenure of the issue would depend on the response of investors to a road show promoting the issue.

"We are planning to launch it in the last week of September or the first week of October," Petronas President Hassan Marican told a news conference after releasing the company's results for the financial year ended March 31, 1996.
Earlier, Petronas said net profit rose 48.3 percent to 6.76 million ringgit for the full year, and that turnover edged up to 22.25 million from 18.09 million ringgit.
"It will be a global issue and the maturity and the amount of the bond will depend on the response from potential investors and also whether it will be in one tranche or two," Hassan said.
He said the road show would last about a week and would be followed by the launch.
"It won't be as extensive as previous road shows," he said, adding that previous Petronas bond issues, two Yankees and a Samurai, had already established the company's profile among investors.
Hassan said he did not expect any complications with the Yankee bond arising from Petronas' investment in Iran's Sirri oil fields.

Petronas last month took a 30 percent stake in two Iranian oil fields being developed by Total SA of France. The investment in the $600 million project puts Malaysia is jeopardy of sanctions from the United States under the Iran-Libya Sanctions Act.
President Bill Clinton signed the act on August 5, which calls for sanctions to be imposed on non-U.S. firms that invest $40 million or more a year in the oil and gas sectors of the two countries.
